Multiple Reference Images will automatically disable the startframe input on WanVideo VACE Start To End Frame.

Set total iterations based on your frame range. Calculate using:
Total Frames / (frames_per_iteration - num_start_frames)

Recommended num_start_frames: 14 ±4.

Other values may produce error frames — if so, check the interpolation section in the subgraph.

- frames_per_iteration = Number of frames generated per iteration. Must follow the Wan formula: 4n+1 (e.g. 41, 45, 49, 53, 57, 61, 65, 69, 73, 77, 81).

- num_start_frames = Number of frames carried over from the previous iteration as context for the current one. These are also the overlap frames, where the different iterations are blended.

- resume_from_iteration = Resume generation from a specific iteration, keeping all previously accumulated frames. Useful for trying different seeds on later iterations without re-running the entire workflow. Set to 0 to start over from scratch.

- total_iterations = Total number of iterations to run. You can start with a lower value, check the result, and then increase it later using resume_from_iteration to continue where you left off.

- seed = Seed value for each sampler. Change these to get different results while keeping everything else fixed.

Use this section to remove and regenerate broken frames at the seam between iterations via interpolation. By default, this feature is disabled - enable it in the Boundary Frame Extractor.

The Extractor picks out the last good frame before the break and the first good frame after it, then feeds that pair into an interpolation node (RIFE, FILM, etc.) which generates smooth replacement frames. The splicer takes those interpolated frames and swaps them back into the video batch in place of the broken ones.
